# Vulnerability details

## Impact
A core function of the juice-buyback contract, which is to maximise the project tokens received by the contributor, won't work whenever a swap from Uniswap V3 pool provides more tokens over minting because the transaction will revert. ## Impact

https://github.com/jbx-protocol/juice-contracts-v3/blob/main/contracts/abstract/JBPayoutRedemptionPaymentTerminal3_1.sol#L1493


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The issue contains 2 parts:

1) The _mint() function has the "if (beneficiaryTokenCount < _minReturnedTokens) revert INADEQUATE_TOKEN_COUNT();" check missing. This check is used to identify whether the beneficiaryTokenCount amount is greater than or equal to the _minReturnedTokens amount desired by the user.

The _mint() function (in line 334 of JBXBuybackDelegate.sol) is called if - (a) the user specifies "_preferClaimedTokens" as false (b) the "_amountReceived" is 0 from the _swap() function. In both cases, the _mint() function is used to mint project tokens to the user. However, after minting the tokens by calling the controller of the project (after line 345), the _mint() function does not check whether "beneficiaryTokenCount" (which is returned by the controller) is greater than or equal to "_minReturnedTokens" (as originally entered by the user in the pay() function).

issues.title: transfer()  method can lead to re-entrancy attack
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L232
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L286


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The contract in scope has a withdraw function namely ‘uniswapV3SwapCallback’ which sends funds to the calling address. The calling address can be a malicious contract. 
Currently transfer() sends more gas than 2300 creating a potential attack vector for re-entrancy.

When the malicious contract call the withdraw function, before reducing the balance of the malicious contract, it's fallback function will be called at it can steal more funds from the contract in scope. 

## Proof of Concept

Check this artilce by Consensys https://consensys.net/diligence/blog/2019/09/stop-using-soliditys-transfer-now/.


## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Recommendation is made for using .call() method which is more gas efficient, as it forwards all remaining gas, as in combination with re-entrancy guard to use after December 2019.
Exception propagation for .call() method can be achieved with a workaround using the re-entrancy Guard Check pattern.
The pattern for Re-entrancy Guard should be by making all state changes before calling other contracts or either using re-entrancy guard modifier.



## Assessed type

Reentrancy

The payParams() function takes the _data parameter, which contains the reservedRate.

JBConstants.MAX_RESERVED_RATE = 10000;

controller.mintTokensOf(..) use _useReservedRate: true

Manual Review /  VSCode

Check the parameter in the payParams() function.
require(_data.reservedRate<MAX_RESERVED_RATE)

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L216
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L271


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Loss of deserved tokens or DoS when users use this contract.

## Proof of Concept
According to the uniswap docs:
https://docs.uniswap.org/contracts/v3/reference/core/interfaces/callback/IUniswapV3SwapCallback#uniswapv3swapcallback

```
The caller of this method must be checked to be a UniswapV3Pool deployed by the canonical UniswapV3Factory.
```

However, there is no check in this contract's implementation. So a malicious user (since anyone can deploy this contract and trick other users into using it) or malicious project owner (not centralization risk I think: https://github.com/code-423n4/2022-10-juicebox-findings/issues/191#issuecomment-1306080547) can create a fake pool, which calls `uniswapV3SwapCallback`. There are two attacks:

1.Reach the max allowed slippage and get extra tokens. The attacker can do the exchange himself at a low slippage but give back the user with a high allowed slippage.

2.Bypass the slippage but revert later. The attacker can pass nice parameters to uniswapv3swapcallback but doesn't transfer tokens (or few), so he can pass the slippage checks. But the transaction will later revert (DoS) either at:

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/9d0458282511ff269b3b35b5b082b56d5cc08663/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L231
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/9d0458282511ff269b3b35b5b082b56d5cc08663/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L183


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
when the contract receives a Uniswap pool callback the contract performs some checks before it proceeds to call the `weth.deposit` with a `msg.value` that is equal to `_amountToSend` to wrap eth and transfer it to the pool, however the contract is not guaranteed to have enough eth to perform this action due to the lack of the `receive()` and `fallback()` functions, the only way the contract can receive funds is from `didPay()` function which can only be called by the `jbxTerminal` this function itself does not check if there is a minimum `msg.value` sent with the function call, this will most likely cause a DoS since the contract can not proceed to call `weth` contract.

## Proof of Concept
the contract does not have any payable functions except the `didPay()` function and cannot receive ETH otherwise

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
consider implementing `receive()` and/or `fallback()` function to make sure the contract won't stop working due to lack of funds.


## Assessed type

DoS

issues.title: Setting the slippage tolerance incorrectly can result in users losing funds
issues.body:
# Lines of code

JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L156


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Since the slippage parameter is also passed from the frontend, we need to validate the magnitude of the parameter value，if slippage  == SLIPPAGE_DENOMINATOR ，users may be vulnerable to sandwich attacks during the Uniswap swapping process, resulting in potential loss of funds

## Proof of Concept
In the code snippet provided in JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L153:

```solidity
// Unpack the quote from the pool, given by the frontend
(,, uint256 _quote, uint256 _slippage) = abi.decode(_data.metadata, (bytes32, bytes32, uint256, uint256));
```

The `_data.metadata` variable in `JBXBuybackDelegate.sol` is obtained from JBSingleTokenPaymentTerminalStore3_1.sol#L367:

```solidity
    JBPayParamsData memory _data = JBPayParamsData(
    IJBSingleTokenPaymentTerminal(msg.sender),
    _payer,
    _amount,
    _projectId,
    fundingCycle.configuration,
    _beneficiary,
    fundingCycle.weight,
    fundingCycle.reservedRate(),
    _memo,
    _metadata
    );
```

`_metadata` is passed in Terminal `pay` function
JBPayoutRedemptionPaymentTerminal3_1.sol#L344#L383

If `_slippage` is equal to `SLIPPAGE_DENOMINATOR`, the `_minimumReceivedFromSwap` value sent to the Uniswap pool is 0, resulting in the loss of user funds.

## Tools Used
vscode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Adding slippage value validation ensures that the slippage remains within a reasonable range, such as being less than 5%


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

issues.title: Should check for `_data.amount.value`
Unsafe cast in swap and uniswapV3SwapCallback functions can lead to attack
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/9d0458282511ff269b3b35b5b082b56d5cc08663/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L224
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/9d0458282511ff269b3b35b5b082b56d5cc08663/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L271


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The swap and uniswapV3SwapCallback functions performs an unsafe cast of a uint256 type to a signed integer.

    _amountReceived = uint256(-(_projectTokenIsZero ? amount0 : amount1));

Note that amount is chosen by the caller and when choosing amount = 2**256 - 1, this is interpreted as 0xFFFFFFFFF... = -1 as a signed integer. Thus -(-1)=1 adds 1 liquidity unit to the position

This allows an attacker to not only swap and send the non-reserved token to the beneficiary, amounts according to the unmodified uint256 amount which is an extremely large value and calculated for _nonReservedToken calculation and is transferred to the beneficiary.

## Proof of Concept
https://solodit.xyz/issues/843

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Even though Solidity 0.8.x is used, type casts do not throw an error.
A SafeCast library must be used everywhere a typecast is done.


## Assessed type

Under/Overflow

issues.title: The return value of an external transfer call is not checked on the function uniswapV3SwapCallback in the contract named JBXBuybackDelegate
`mintedAmount` and `reservedRate` mutex not working
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L101-L113


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

```solidity
File: JBXBuybackDelegate.sol
101     /**
102      * @notice The amount of token created if minted is prefered
103      *
104      * @dev    This is a mutex 1-x-1
105      */
106     uint256 private mintedAmount = 1;
107
108     /**
109      * @notice The current reserved rate
110      *
111      * @dev    This is a mutex 1-x-1
112      */
113     uint256 private reservedRate = 1;
```

`mintedAmount` and `reservedRate` are designed as mutual exclusion locks to ensure that the `payParams` function and the `didPay` function are corresponding. But in the implementation, these two mutexes don't seem to work. This causes two users to use the `JBXBuybackDelegate` contract at the same time, `payParams` function and `didPay` function may be confused.

## Proof of Concept

1. UserA call `payParams`
2. UserB call `payParams`
3. UserA call `didPay` and use the UserB's `mintedAmount` and `reservedRate`
4. UserB call `didPay` and use the default `mintedAmount` and `reservedRate`

## Tools Used

## Impact
The contract fails to adequately validate and sanitize the _data parameters passed to several critical functions, which can allow for malicious or unexpected inputs. This lack of input validation can lead to the following potential vulnerabilities:

Input Manipulation:
An attacker could exploit the absence of input validation to manipulate the _data parameter, providing unexpected or malicious values. This could potentially lead to unintended consequences or exploitation of vulnerabilities within the contract.

Integer Overflow/Underflow:
Without proper input validation, the contract may perform calculations or operations using the input data without verifying their range or size. This can result in integer overflow or underflow, leading to incorrect calculations or unexpected behaviors. An attacker may leverage this vulnerability to manipulate the contract's state or exploit other vulnerabilities.

Unexpected Behaviors:
Insufficient input validation may result in unexpected behaviors or corner cases that the contract does not handle properly. This can create vulnerabilities that an attacker could exploit to gain unauthorized access, manipulate the contract's behavior, or disrupt its intended functionality.

issues.title: On-chain slippage calculation can be manipulated and lead to MEV / sandwich attacks
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L197


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

beneficiary can get less tokens than expected.

## Proof of Concept

In `didPay` method of `JBXBuybackDelegate.sol`, `_data` is passed from `jbxTerminal`.

```solidity
File: JBXBuybackDelegate.sol

183:    function didPay(JBDidPayData calldata _data) external payable override {

196:    (,, uint256 _quote, uint256 _slippage) = abi.decode(_data.metadata, (bytes32, bytes32, uint256, uint256));
197:    uint256 _minimumReceivedFromSwap = _quote - (_quote * _slippage / SLIPPAGE_DENOMINATOR);

```
[Link to Code](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-05-juicebox/blob/main/juice-buyback/contracts/JBXBuybackDelegate.sol#L197)

As per the Natspec, the `_quote` values passed is the `Uniswap quote` data for that pool.

This opens up the attack vector:

The `_quote` value which is the uniswap quote value is vulnerable to price manipulation attacks. A malicious actor can execute a sandwich attack, which will:

* manipulate the price of a Uniswap pool that swaps a project token;
* swapping of tokens happens at a manipulated price, which will be lower than the market price;
* return the amount in the pool back, profiting from the project tokens sold below the market price.

Here as `minimumReceivedFromSwap` is calculated on chain, the complete attack scenario becomes deterministic which can be exploited easily by MEV Bot.

## Tools Used

VS Code

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

It is always recommended to let beneficiary set the `minimumReceivedFromSwap` parameter directly and avoid on chain calculations of such parameter. The value should be calculated off-chain by the caller before the transaction is sent–this doesn't allow MEV bots to manipulate the price.


## Assessed type

MEV
